title: Cap. X Arg. V: therefore election/predestination and preterition/reprobation do not hang on antecedent foresight of faith or unbelief — they precede such foresight
latin: Electio sive praedestinatio, et praeteritio sive reprobatio non pendent ex praevisione antecedanea fidei et perseverantiae in quibusdam, ac infidelitatis et pertinaciae in aliis, sed talem praevisionem antecedunt.
pass_a: Election or predestination, and preterition or reprobation, do not hang from antecedent foresight of faith and of perseverance in certain ones, and of unbelief and of pertinacity in others, but precede such foresight.
pass_b: So election — that is, predestination — and preterition — that is, reprobation — do not hang on antecedent foresight of faith and perseverance in some, and of unbelief and pertinacity in others. They precede that foresight.

title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: John x. 28–29 — the Father gave Christ certain sheep no force can snatch; giving = electing singular persons to defend and lead infallibly to eternal life
latin: Majoris veritas ex hisce Scripturarum testimoniis patet; Joann. x. 28, 29. Nemo rapit oves meas de manu mea. Pater meus, qui eas dedit mihi, major omnibus est: neque quisquam potest eas rapere e manu Patris mei. Quaero quis sensus horum verborum, Pater Christo dedit oves certas, quas nulla vis potest rapere, nisi, Deus Pater eligendo dedit Christo singulares quasdam personas, quas decrevit contra omnes carnis, mundi, et diaboli impetus insidiasque defendere, atque tandem ad fruitionem aeternae vitae infallibiliter perducere?
pass_a: The truth of the Major is plain from these testimonies of the Scriptures; Joann. x. 28, 29. No one snatches my sheep out of my hand. My Father, who gave them unto me, is greater than all: neither can anyone snatch them out of my Father's hand. I ask what is the sense of these words, The Father gave unto Christ certain sheep, which no force can snatch, except that God the Father by electing gave unto Christ certain singular persons, whom he decreed to defend against all the assaults and snares of the flesh, the world, and the devil, and at length infallibly to lead unto the fruition of everlasting life?
pass_b: The Major's truth is plain from these Scripture witnesses (John x. 28–29): No one snatches my sheep out of my hand. My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all; and no one can snatch them out of my Father's hand. What sense have the words The Father gave Christ certain sheep that no force can snatch — unless this: God the Father, by electing, gave Christ certain singular persons, whom he decreed to defend against all assaults and snares of flesh, world, and devil, and at last to lead infallibly to the fruition of everlasting life?

lemmas.gloss: Father gave Christ certain sheep none can snatch
giving = electing to defend and lead to life

title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: not to be given to Christ by the Father = not ordained by that gracious decree to obtain eternal life in and through Christ; John xvii. 9; Eph. i. 4–5
latin: E contra, quid est non dari Christo a Patre, nisi tali gratioso decreto ad vitam aeternam in Christo et per Christum infallibiliter obtinendam minime ordinari? Quo etiam spectant illa verba, Joann. xvii. 9. Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro iis quos dedisti mihi, quia tui sunt. Sunt igitur quidam non-dati Christo, non numerati in peculio Dei Patris, hoc est, non-electi antequam jacerentur mundi fundamenta, non-praedestinati in adoptionem filiorum pro benevolo affectu voluntatis Divinae, Eph. i. 4, 5, etc.
pass_a: On the contrary, what is it not to be given unto Christ by the Father, except by no means to be ordained by such a gracious decree unto everlasting life to be infallibly obtained in Christ and through Christ? Unto which also those words look, Joann. xvii. 9. I ask not for the world, but for those whom thou hast given me, because they are thine. There are therefore certain ones not-given unto Christ, not numbered in the peculiar flock of God the Father, that is, non-elect before the foundations of the world were laid, not-predestined unto the adoption of sons according to the benevolent affection of the Divine will, Eph. i. 4, 5, etc.
pass_b: On the contrary: what is it not to be given to Christ by the Father, except this — not to be ordained by that gracious decree to obtain everlasting life infallibly in Christ and through Christ? Those words look the same way (John xvii. 9): I ask not for the world, but for those whom you have given me, because they are yours. So there are some not-given to Christ, not numbered in God the Father's peculiar flock — that is, non-elect before the world's foundations were laid, not predestined to the adoption of sons according to the benevolent affection of the divine will (Eph. i. 4–5, etc.).

lemmas.gloss: not-given = not ordained to eternal life in Christ

title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine — those given to Christ are ordained to eternal life, predestined and called according to purpose, none of whom perish; given = elect; not-given = reprobate/passed over
latin: Augustino haec praedictorum verborum semper placuit sententia: Hi Christo intelliguntur dari, qui ordinati sunt in vitam aeternam. Ipsi sunt illi praedestinati, et secundum propositum vocati, quorum nullus perit, De corr. et grat. cap. 9. Et in Evang. Joann. Tractat. 106. Quos Deus Filius de mundo elegit cum Patre, idem ipse homo Filius de mundo accepit a Patre. Non enim Pater illos Filio dedisset, nisi elegisset. Videtis igitur per datos Christo, ex mente Augustini, nil aliud intelligi, quam electos sive praedestinatos: Et e contra, per non-datos intelligi reprobatos, hoc est, praeteritos et minime praedestinatos, apud eundem Augustinum aeque in confesso est.
pass_a: Unto Augustine this sentence of the aforesaid words was always pleasing: These are understood to be given unto Christ, who are ordained unto everlasting life. They themselves are those predestined, and called according to purpose, of whom none perishes, De corr. et grat. cap. 9. And in Evang. Joann. Tractat. 106. Those whom God the Son elected from the world with the Father, the same himself as man the Son received from the world from the Father. For the Father would not have given them unto the Son, unless he had elected them. You see therefore that by those given unto Christ, from Augustine's mind, nothing else is understood than the elect or predestined: And on the contrary, that by the not-given the reprobate are understood, that is, the passed over and by no means predestined, is equally confessed with the same Augustine.
pass_b: Augustine always liked this reading of those words: These are understood as given to Christ who are ordained to everlasting life. They are the predestined, and called according to purpose, of whom none perishes (De corr. et grat. cap. 9). And in Tract. 106 on John's Gospel: Those whom God the Son elected from the world with the Father, the same as man the Son received from the world from the Father. For the Father would not have given them to the Son unless he had elected them. So you see: by those given to Christ, on Augustine's mind, nothing else is meant than the elect or predestined. And on the contrary, by the not-given the reprobate are meant — that is, the passed over and not predestined — which Augustine equally confesses.

lemmas.lemma: Hi Christo ... dari, qui ordinati sunt
lemmas.gloss: Augustine: given = ordained to eternal life

title: Cap. X Arg. V Major: Augustine Tract. 107/111 — world = those not in the lot of grace to be chosen out of it; those not given are those to whom Christ will not give eternal life = the passed-over alone
latin: Hinc Tract. 107. in Evang. Joann. ad haec verba, Non pro mundo rogo, sed pro his quos dedisti mihi, sic scribit; Mundum vult intelligi, qui vivunt secundum concupiscentiam mundi, et non sunt in ea sorte gratiae ut ab illo eligantur ex mundo. Et Tract. 111: Non ei dati sunt, quibus vitam non dabit aeternam. At quinam tandem illi sunt, quibus Christus non dabit vitam aeternam, nisi illi, et illi soli, quos appellamus praeteritos, non-electos sive reprobatos? nam omnibus electis dabit eam.
pass_a: Hence Tract. 107. in Evang. Joann. unto these words, I ask not for the world, but for these whom thou hast given me, he so writes; He wills the world to be understood as those who live according to the concupiscence of the world, and are not in that lot of grace that they be elected by him out of the world. And Tract. 111: They have not been given unto him, unto whom he will not give everlasting life. But who finally are those, unto whom Christ will not give everlasting life, except those, and those alone, whom we call the passed over, non-elect or reprobate? for unto all the elect he will give it.
pass_b: Hence on Tract. 107 on John's Gospel, at the words I ask not for the world, but for these whom you have given me, he writes: By world he means those who live by the world's lust, and are not in that lot of grace to be chosen by him out of the world. And Tract. 111: They have not been given to him to whom he will not give everlasting life. But who finally are those to whom Christ will not give everlasting life, except those — and those alone — whom we call the passed over, non-elect or reprobate? For to all the elect he will give it.

lemmas.gloss: world = not in grace-lot to be chosen out
not given eternal life = passed-over alone

title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor: given/not-given distinction precedes human faith and perseverance — John vi. 37: coming to Christ depends on the Father's giving as antecedent cause
latin: Veniamus nunc ad Minorem, et ostendamus hanc distinctionem datorum et non-datorum Christo antecedere fidem et perseverantiam humanam, antecedere etiam praevisionem absolutam infidelitatis et pertinaciae humanae. Quod fidem et perseverantiam antecedat ex illis verbis colligitur, Quicquid mihi dat Pater, ad me veniet: et eum qui venit ad me non ejiciam foras, Joann. vi. 37. Manifestum est ex hisce verbis, venire ad Christum et permanere in Christo, quod est credere in Christum et in fide perseverare, ex hac datione Patris, tanquam ex antecedente causa dependere.
pass_a: Let us now come unto the Minor, and show that this discrimination of those given and not-given unto Christ precedes human faith and perseverance, precedes also absolute foresight of human unbelief and pertinacity. That it precedes faith and perseverance is gathered from those words, Whatsoever the Father gives me shall come unto me: and him who comes unto me I will not cast out, Joann. vi. 37. It is manifest from these words that to come unto Christ and to remain in Christ, which is to believe in Christ and to persevere in faith, depends from this giving of the Father, as from an antecedent cause.
pass_b: Now to the Minor: let us show that this distinction of those given and not-given to Christ precedes human faith and perseverance, and also precedes absolute foresight of human unbelief and pertinacity. That it precedes faith and perseverance is gathered from these words: Whatever the Father gives me will come to me; and him who comes to me I will not cast out (John vi. 37). From those words it is plain: coming to Christ and remaining in Christ — that is, believing in Christ and persevering in faith — depends on this giving of the Father as on an antecedent cause.

lemmas.gloss: coming to Christ depends on Father's prior giving

title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor: John xvii. 6, 15, 24 and Matt. xiii. 11 — order: persons given to Christ first; then Spirit opens hearts to faith; then he sustains them; God does not elect from foresight of free-will faith
latin: Idem patet Joann. xvii. 6. Ubi Christus dicit se manifestasse nomen Patris sui hominibus, quos dedit illi de mundo. Et vers. 15. Rogat specialim pro hisce, ut serventur a malo illo, et ad gloriam aeternam perducantur vers. 24. Huc etiam faciunt illa verba Matth. xiii. 11. Vobis datum est nosse mysteria regni caelorum, illis non est datum. In quibus locis ipse ordo est diligenter observandus. Primo, certae quaedam personae dantur Christo vivificandae et salvandae ex speciali beneplacito Dei Patris. Tum Christus speciali operatione Spiritus sui aperit horum corda, ut salutiferam Dei cognitionem ac fidem concipiant. Tandem illuminatos et conversos ita gubernat et sustentat, ut nullis diaboli tentationibus ad interitum seducantur. Non ergo speculatur Deus quinam sunt libero suo arbitrio per gratiam excitato credituri et perseveraturi, et ex hac praevisione aliis praeteritis eos eligit, sed eligit quosdam ex mero suo beneplacito, donatque Christo, quibus Christus inspirat fidem ut accedant ad Deum, et indit perseverantiam ne recedant ab eo.
pass_a: The same is plain Joann. xvii. 6. Where Christ says that he has manifested the name of his Father unto the men whom he gave him from the world. And vers. 15. He asks specially for these, that they be kept from that evil one, and unto everlasting glory be led vers. 24. Unto this also those words of Matth. xiii. 11. avail. Unto you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of the heavens, unto them it is not given. In which places the order itself is diligently to be observed. First, certain persons are given unto Christ to be quickened and saved from the special good pleasure of God the Father. Then Christ by a special operation of his Spirit opens these ones' hearts, that they may conceive saving knowledge of God and faith. At length he so governs and sustains the illuminated and converted that by no temptations of the devil they be seduced unto destruction. God therefore does not look to see who by their free choice excited by grace will believe and persevere, and from this foresight elect them, others being passed over, but he elects certain ones from his mere good pleasure, and gives them unto Christ, unto whom Christ inspires faith that they may approach unto God, and implants perseverance that they may not withdraw from him.
pass_b: The same is plain in John xvii. 6, where Christ says he has manifested his Father's name to the men the Father gave him from the world. And verse 15: he asks specially for these, that they be kept from that evil one, and led to everlasting glory (verse 24). Matthew xiii. 11 serves the same point: To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven; to them it is not given. In these places the order itself must be carefully watched. First, certain persons are given to Christ to be quickened and saved from God the Father's special good pleasure. Then Christ, by a special operation of his Spirit, opens their hearts so they conceive saving knowledge of God and faith. At last he so governs and sustains the illuminated and converted that no devil's temptations seduce them to ruin. God does not look to see who by free choice excited by grace will believe and persevere, and from that foresight elect them while passing others over. He elects some from his mere good pleasure, and gives them to Christ; Christ inspires faith in them that they may come to God, and implants perseverance that they may not withdraw from him.

lemmas.gloss: not elect from foresight of free-will faith

title: Cap. X Arg. V Minor close: Augustine Tract. 105 — the Son is glorified so as to make the Father known to all given him; being given to Christ (that is, elected) is prior to knowing
latin: Audiamus eundem quem antea audivimus Augustinum; Sic se Filium glorificat, ut omnibus quos dedisti ei te cognitum faciat, Tract. 105. in Evang. Joann. Est igitur prius Christo donari a Patre, hoc est eligi, quam cognoscere.
pass_a: Let us hear the same Augustine whom we heard before; So he glorifies the Son, that unto all whom thou hast given him he may make thee known, Tract. 105. in Evang. Joann. It is therefore prior to be given unto Christ by the Father, that is to be elected, than to know.
pass_b: Hear again the same Augustine: So he glorifies the Son, that to all whom you have given him he may make you known (Tract. 105. on John's Gospel). Therefore being given to Christ by the Father — that is, being elected — is prior to knowing.
